fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: October's 165,000 jobs against 65,000 forecast and a 0.3% rise in core consumer prices turned the committee hawkish: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan wants two more hikes, possibly rapidly, and Waller has hardened too. At stake is a half-point move rather than a quarter, and whether Warsh answers the credibility doubts his October messaging revived.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Atlanta's foreign ministers' meeting ended with no group photo, after Europeans refused to stand beside Lavrov, and no joint statement. The EU's Kallas said hosting Putin risks normalising war crimes; Rubio defended Russia's seat and floated a Black Sea ceasefire. The summit tests whether the US presidency can keep both in the room.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Eurozone inflation has hit 4%, above 2% for eight straight months, and Nagel has backed a December hike that would be the third this year; Panetta has said more may be needed. Lagarde leaves on 7 February, so this is among her last decisions while Knot and De Cos vie to succeed her.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The Bank of England has just raised rates and forecast that Britain's inflation will peak at 4.9%. Bailey has said a second hike is more likely than not if the war goes on, so this meeting turns on whether the war and the prices it is pushing up have eased by the time the committee sits.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Tokyo spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, with markets fully pricing a December Fed hike, while nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raised profit forecasts on the weak yen. This meeting settles whether the rate joins intervention in defending a currency that exporters are profiting from.

fred-us-ppi-2026-11-13.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Producer Price Index, which measures what US businesses receive for goods and services before they reach shoppers. It is an early read on cost pressure that feeds into consumer prices and Fed thinking.
fred-us-ppi-2026-11-13.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the US PPI for the latest month, settling how fast prices at the factory gate and in wholesale trade moved before they pass to consumers.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-11-17.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly early estimate of what US retailers and restaurants sold. Consumer spending drives most of the American economy, so the figure moves Treasury yields, the dollar and expectations for interest rates.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-11-17.recent: The Census Bureau reports another month of US spending at stores, restaurants and online sellers, settling how much demand households carried into the year-end shopping season.
